1) bacteria are an important trophic resource for invertebrate consumers in a detritus-based stream food web, especially in the absence of leaf litter inputs, 2) bacterial carbon is a significant proportion of the carbon assimilated by invertebrates, and 3) bacteria are a significant proportion of carbon assimilated by aquatic insects.
bacteria were the most important trophic link between DOC and invertebrates in a headwater stream.
bacteria are an important food source for stream invertebrates and that bacteria are an especially important food source when other food sources (such as leaf litter) are scarce.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of bacteria as an important component of detritus-based stream food webs.
the trophic role of bacteria in a detritus-based stream food web, and the effect of detritus on bacterial production.
the trophic role of bacteria in a detritus-based food web.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bacteria are a trophically important link in the food chain in these streams.
bacteria were a significant trophic component in the food webs of both streams, but that bacteria were relatively more important in the litter-exclusion stream than in the reference stream.
bacteria are a significant trophic link between DOC and consumers in these streams, and the importance of bacteria is increased in the absence of leaf litter inputs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bacteria are important in stream food webs, especially in streams that are low in leaf litter inputs.
the bacteria in a detritus-based food web are important consumers of streamwater DOC, and that they are a significant trophic resource for invertebrates.

the trophic importance of bacteria to in-stream consumers in a leaf-litter-dominated headwater stream is relatively minor, but that bacteria may play a more important role in a stream that is low in leaf-litter-derived DOC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bacteria are an important component in the food web of headwater streams and can be a substantial source of energy for invertebrate consumers.
bacteria can contribute a large portion of the diet of invertebrates in streams with low leaf litter input.
